head: 1b31e607608331b97f7f15427b0ec935e739a707
summary: Gemma 4 12B IT w4a16 served by vLLM 0.26 in WSL2; all Stage 1 contract items exercised over HTTP
result: All nine items pass. Weights 8.28 GiB, KV cache 11.79 GiB / 92403 tokens, TTFT 0.39 s, text 1.13 s, image 1.22 s, tool call 0.72 s, structured JSON 1.57 s. Speech untested; peak VRAM not measurable via nvidia-smi because vLLM preallocates 0.9 of the card.
decision: Endpoint is viable for Stage 1. Keep VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 and VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 under WSL. Take VRAM figures from the vLLM startup log, never from nvidia-smi.

head: 1b31e607608331b97f7f15427b0ec935e739a707
summary: Speech input verified on Gemma 4 12B IT w4a16 via the vLLM endpoint
result: 8.68 s stereo 24 kHz FLAC = 215 audio tokens; verbatim transcript correct in 1.19 s; language and speaker tone identified correctly. Synthetic tones remain unreliable: a 440 Hz sine is called laughter at temperature 0 while a sweep is described correctly.
decision: Audio is speech-oriented and usable as-is. Do not extrapolate audio quality to non-speech sound. The sample stays outside the repository; a committable speech fixture is still needed.

head: 1b31e607608331b97f7f15427b0ec935e739a707
summary: Stage 1 smoke script: repository code drives every contract item against the local Gemma 4 endpoint
result: 9 of 9 checks pass with content assertions, not just status codes: text 0.27 s, system prompt 0.08 s, streaming 0.38 s (TTFT 0.04 s, 20 chunks), single image 0.12 s, two images 0.22 s, speech wav 0.25 s, speech flac 0.22 s, tool call 0.37 s, structured JSON 0.65 s. 42 offline tests pass without a server. Three first-run failures were real: unbounded numeric fields make guided decoding repeat digits until max_tokens is exhausted (fixed by minimum/maximum, 8.63 s unparsable -> 0.65 s correct); a 20 ms tone let a liveness check pass while the model received no audio; a (220,20,20) circle is called pink.
decision: Stage 1 closes. Every JSON schema this project sends must bound its numeric fields. Audio fixtures must carry speech, not synthetic tone.

head: 14036d0a38f68be80d42e382dbc6855f22ebc09f
summary: Can LangGraph be used without adopting LangChain types? Measured against langgraph 1.2.10 in a throwaway environment.
result: Core StateGraph ran a two-iteration tool loop on the project's own frozen dataclasses and restored 4 messages for a thread from InMemorySaver; langgraph.types.interrupt is present for confirmation gates. The prebuilts refuse: create_react_agent's signature requires a langchain_core BaseChatModel or Runnable, and ToolNode inside a graph accepted a langchain_core AIMessage but rejected the project's dataclass with NotImplementedError: Unsupported message type. langgraph 1.2.10 depends on langchain-core<2,>=1.4.7 regardless, so langchain_core is installed either way. One caveat found: checkpointing unregistered custom classes warns 'this will be blocked in a future version', so graph state should hold JSON-able structures or register its types.
decision: Use LangGraph core with the project's own message type; write the tool loop by hand. Do not use create_react_agent or ToolNode. See DECISIONS.md 2026-08-01.

head: 4c5663ab42a3e4ce4f40bfc2eebcf3da4d914822
summary: The tool loop closes: a two-node LangGraph graph drives a real call-tool-answer cycle on the project's own Message type
result: Live run against gemma-4-12b-it on vLLM: the model chose list_files{path=.}, then read_file{path=README.md}, then answered from the file contents. Two tool iterations, seven messages, 3.82 s end to end. vLLM accepted an assistant turn with content null plus tool_calls, and the tool-role replies carrying tool_call_id. Offline: 72 tests pass, 30 of them new.
decision: Assistant turns serialize with content null when they only call tools. Tool failures are returned to the model as tool messages rather than raised, so a mistyped path costs a turn instead of the run. Loop bounding is left to LangGraph's recursion limit; no counter in the graph.

head: 3600757d3e99773722224e55f7efc90547e2ef70
summary: Stage 2: four-node LangGraph agent with tools, SQLite memory and a rolling summary, run live against vLLM
result: Two sessions in one run, 10.0 s for eight model calls: remember_fact and list_files in session one, search_memory in a new thread after reopening the store, summary written covering positions 0-11 with all 18 messages still stored. 137 offline tests pass.
decision: Stage 2 closed; Stage 3 grows the same graph with checkpoints and interrupt rather than replacing it

head: a0c92af5d93d5ec8029c32a79abf6d1ee76c3374
summary: Stage 3 first step: checkpoints, resumable turns, and confirmation before a destructive tool
result: Live: the model called write_file, the turn stopped with nothing written, the agent was closed and reopened, the same question came back with its id and arguments intact, approving wrote the file and declining left it alone with the refusal reaching the model. Whole flow 4.0 s. 156 offline tests pass, up from 137.
decision: A tool declares itself destructive and the graph asks; without a checkpointer there is nowhere to wait, so the call is declined rather than run

head: 012a3d997eec713166365eb77a466008f732d642
summary: Version 1 live check against vLLM: token budget from the server, a fold triggered by measured request size, the thread list, and a dead endpoint
result: context_limit 16384 from /v1/models, budget 9830 at fraction 0.6; one real turn 470/9830 tokens in 0.5 s; at fraction 0.02 (budget 327) three short turns used 468/483/513 tokens and folded through 0 -> 2 -> 4 with a readable summary and no message lost; two threads listed with their openings; a dead endpoint cost 3 attempts and 6.3 s and named itself

head: 584d3285cb02380817b1efc74df02c4866bcc4c5
summary: Cold start and latency of the deployed Gemma 4 12B endpoint on a Modal A10
result: First boot ~196s container-start to listening (init engine 127s, compilation 78s). Idle-to-answer with warm compile cache 201s: 197s wake plus 3.7s answer. Second boot init engine 62s, compilation 17.7s. Weights 6.9s / 8.28 GiB. Warm answer 1.8-2.4s for 24 output tokens, ~13 tok/s. KV cache 10.03 GiB of 22.06 GiB device memory; vLLM offers 11.6 GiB. Scale to zero confirmed by 86 consecutive 503s while no container existed.
decision: Accept the numbers and keep max_model_len at 16384 for now. The wake is dominated by container scheduling and image pull, not compilation, so optimization should target the image rather than torch.compile.

head: ade2ad66beef43e0a7cd027738a6e7625bc521f9
summary: assistant-llm-v2 snapshot boot on A10 at gpu-memory-utilization 0.80
result: KV cache 11.06 GiB; vLLM start to healthy 170.2s; fall asleep 2.74s; 8.39 GiB backed to CPU and 11.12 GiB KV discarded; wake from snapshot 1.00s; resume healthy 0.0s; warm /v1/models 0.88s; warm chat completion 1.31s for 18 in / 25 out
decision: Keep 0.80 and snapshots; measure a genuine restored cold start before claiming any cold-start improvement

head: a39d5fe3c9b246c43737c05bfff31a07f392c7b5
summary: First restored cold start of assistant-llm-v2 after scale-to-zero
result: request-to-serving 25.0s vs baseline 189-201s; text warm 1.67s 15.0 tok/s; image warm 3.81s correct; audio failed 500 (vllm[audio] missing, fixed pending redeploy); bearer token accepted on .modal.run
decision: Snapshot delivers the intended cold-start reduction; redeploy the audio fix and take a second restored wake before treating this as acceptance-grade

head: 770f43bf454a655808f03b30b99c28d8986dd70d
summary: Audio-capable snapshot rebuild and restore observation
result: The first request after the image change rebuilt the GPU snapshot: vLLM healthy in 162.2s, then restored and served the queued request in a 23.8s restore/serve phase. Text, image and audio endpoints returned HTTP 200 in 0.71s, 1.50s and 4.53s; final audio semantic assertion was lost with the detached client exit code. Container scaled to zero.
decision: Do not count this as the second independent restored wake. Run one separately authorized strict measurement against the new snapshot and retain its exit code; monitor the post-restore NCCL TCPStore warning.

head: d0c52ed98fae811694cdb24c433ad2fccb451323
summary: Strict multimodal wake after audio snapshot rebuild
result: Single request completed exit 0. Modal rebuilt another GPU snapshot: request-to-serving 446.5 s. Text 1.64 s at 15.2 tok/s, image 2.75 s, audio 5.03 s; all semantic checks passed. Eventual scale-to-zero confirmed. NCCL TCPStore Broken pipe warnings repeated.
decision: Do not run another identical paid wake. Diagnose snapshot variant selection and reuse from documentation and retained logs first.

head: d0c52ed98fae811694cdb24c433ad2fccb451323
summary: Correction: first container failed during strict wake
result: Modal dashboard marked the first container Failed. The single pending client request was continued by Modal on another container, which rebuilt the snapshot and passed text/image/audio after 446.5 s. CLI logs show repeated NCCL TCPStore Broken pipe warnings but no definitive fatal traceback for the first container.
decision: Treat 446.5 s as failed-container plus platform-retry plus successful snapshot-build time. Diagnose the failure and snapshot reuse before another paid invocation.

head: d0c52ed98fae811694cdb24c433ad2fccb451323
summary: Final 60-second restored-wake control
result: One authorized A10 wake reused the audio-capable snapshot. Client request-to-serving 10.4 s; Modal route 8.64 s with 15 ms execution; resume healthy after 0.0 s; text 1.47 s at 17.0 tok/s; exit 0; no snapshot creation; scale-to-zero confirmed after 35 s. NCCL TCPStore Broken pipe warnings repeated every second around restore and idle.
decision: Snapshot reuse is proven; no more identical paid wakes. Investigate and suppress the NCCL log spam separately using current documentation and retained logs.

head: 95d2d911a1092ec5b7cfb10c63960b0f8f59cc8d
summary: Real Telegram turn through assistant-llm-v2
result: Passed: one restored A10 container served the shared harness's two completion calls in 17.8s and 1.66s; the human received the Telegram reply. vLLM wake was 0.951s, resume health 0.0s, and scale-to-zero was confirmed.
decision: Close V2 step 3b. Keep NCCL warnings until the next independently necessary deploy. Step 2 still needs a bounded work request through Telegram.

head: 95d2d911a1092ec5b7cfb10c63960b0f8f59cc8d
summary: Attribute final Telegram acceptance cost
result: Modal Billing exposed .20093184 for all assistant-llm-v2 activity in the 08:00 hourly bucket; the roughly 63-second Telegram test is estimated at .0207 including CPU and memory, not an exact per-request charge.
decision: Record hourly truth and label the per-test value as an estimate; do not claim exact request-level billing.

head: a9586fe833f6366884ec66a018bca5f1bdade941
summary: Neon pooled control-plane live acceptance
result: Conversation contract 25 passed in 88.96s; migration 15.7s; inbox/checkpointer smoke 1 passed in 13.34s; GPU/VRAM 0.
decision: Accept pooled Neon for the control plane after replacing session search_path with transaction-local schema selection and normalizing LangGraph to public.

head: ad268c2d98ff2e5bd1c3670b7985ca70bd77b790
summary: Measured first deployed warm Neon context read
result: eu-south-2 returned correct 8-message/3-prelude shape, but warm samples were 749.049, 640.399, 648.692, 641.838, and 961.732 ms; warm max 961.732 ms failed the 100 ms gate. Neon server execution shown by the human was only 0.1-6.7 ms.
decision: Keep the control-plane stage open. Remove runtime migrations and collapse complete PostgreSQL read/write boundaries to one network flush before retrying.

head: 1c1e2312d1dbe6c789d295caffbfd39b0533995d
summary: Control-plane warm database read latency after the round-trip correction, Modal eu-south-2 to Neon us-east-2
result: Warm samples 109.815, 109.481, 109.421, 109.389, 218.004 ms; warm max 218.004 ms against a 100 ms limit; cold 1008.954 ms against 500 ms, not accepted as database-cold because Neon idleness was unconfirmed. Previous warm max was 961.732 ms, so the correction is an 8.8x improvement and four of five samples agree within 0.4 ms at 109.4 ms. Server-side execution for the whole workload is about 5 ms, so 109 ms is one trans-Atlantic round trip: the read is now a single round trip and the code is no longer the bottleneck.
decision: The gate stays open and cannot be passed by code: the 100 ms limit is below the 109 ms geographic floor. Two follow-ups: identify the occasional second round trip that produced the 218 ms sample, then decide placement, since both ends on one continent bring the same read to roughly 5-30 ms.

head: 1c1e2312d1dbe6c789d295caffbfd39b0533995d
summary: A/B of two Neon databases from one Modal container: us-east-2 versus eu-central-1
result: Container landed in us-east-2. Primary (Neon us-east-2) warm 2.764, 2.677, 2.243, 2.120, 3.442 ms, warm max 3.442 ms, cold 111.831 ms. Alternate (Neon eu-central-1) warm 98.796, 98.699, 99.038, 98.877, 196.902 ms, warm max 196.902 ms, cold 707.602 ms. Both returned the expected fixture shape. Co-located warm latency is 30x under the 100 ms limit and cold is under the 500 ms limit. The previous 109 ms reading came from the same primary database measured from eu-south-2, so two invocations of one deployed function landed on two continents.
decision: Do not move the database. The database is correctly placed and the worker is not: unpinned Modal placement is the defect, and pinning the control functions to the database's region is what closes the gate. Migrating the primary to Frankfurt would have turned a 3.4 ms result into a 98.7-196.9 ms failure. The region price multiplier for the US region should be checked before assuming pinning costs anything. The fifth-sample outlier is confirmed as exactly one extra round trip, periodic across three runs, and is a millisecond when co-located.

head: cce604deeab82e785462f2c7f19b7d32379dbda5
summary: Telegram webhook latency after the async spawn and a 15 s scaledown window
result: Before, every message: duration 5.05/4.67/4.75 s, execution 1.85/1.67/1.78 s, each with Modal's AsyncUsageWarning. After, cold: 4.69 s duration, 1.70 s execution. After, warm: 306.2 ms duration, 271.4 ms execution — 15x faster on the warm path. Human's own account: first message about ten seconds, second nearly instant. Remaining cold cost: ~3.0 s container start, ~1.4 s of first-execution imports and the first Neon TLS handshake, an unmeasured worker cold start, and a 5.5 s GPU wake.
decision: Keep 15 s on the webhook and worker and 2 s on the probe: a cold start costs about three seconds of a person's attention while a full window costs $0.000066 and $0.00026, so the expensive resource here is the person, the opposite of the GPU case. The two fixes cannot be separated by this data — the cold path did not move, so the visible win is the window and no isolated gain is claimed for the async spawn. min_containers=1 would remove about 4.4 s of the cold path for about $11 a month; recorded as a priced option, not a recommendation.

head: c75187f2646edcee1f8b3abee4bec189f28d3c1d
summary: Webhook import cost, before and after removing the agent stack
result: Local venv, warm cache: the webhook path imported in ~750 ms and loaded langgraph, langchain_core, langsmith and app.agent; after the split it imports in ~223 ms with none of them present. Image-relevant install is ~100 MB, of which the Modal client is ~25 MB, cryptography ~11 MB and psycopg ~14 MB; the agent stack a split image would drop is ~16 MB.
decision: Keep one image and rely on lazy imports plus a memory snapshot; a slim webhook image would buy the imports already bought, not the 3.0 s container start.

head: c75187f2646edcee1f8b3abee4bec189f28d3c1d
summary: First deployed numbers for the snapshotted webhook
result: Three cold starts each created a snapshot instead of reusing one: 11.5 s, 8.87 s and 9.31 s total against 4.69 s unsnapshotted. Execution alone fell from 1.70 s to 0.94-1.40 s. One request that landed on an already-restored container took 1.30 s total, 1.16 s execution.
decision: Keep the flag: creation is documented as first-invocation behaviour because snapshots are per worker type, and the converged case is what matters. Revert if cold starts still log Creating after about ten of them.

head: c75187f2646edcee1f8b3abee4bec189f28d3c1d
summary: Memory snapshot on the webhook, measured over nine deployed cold starts
result: Mean cold: 5.36 s before snapshots, 8.56 s while creating (6 of 9), 4.06 s restoring. Execution fell 1.67-3.86 s to 0.34-0.46 s and warm 271 ms to ~200 ms from the import change alone. Subtracting execution leaves ~3.5 s of container in both the snapshot and no-snapshot cases.
decision: Revert enable_memory_snapshot; keep the import split. A restore skips initialization, and removing the agent stack from the webhook's imports had already removed the initialization, so the two were substitutes. The residual ~3.5 s is Modal scheduling and only min_containers removes it.

head: e9563c622e98a5c0e4f367fe823062ca29b167b0
summary: Update worker cold start, from the Modal startup column
result: Scheduling 3.23 s (3.05-3.36). Cold execution 3.99 s against 2.28 s warm, so 1.71 s of first-execution initialization. Total 4.93 s over a warm worker, the largest CPU number in the first-message chain.
decision: Raise the worker idle window to 60 s to match the webhook, about $3/month at a hundred wakes a day. Hold the module-scope-imports-plus-snapshot option, worth about 1.2 s, until the wider window shows how often a cold worker still happens.

head: f9edc7ca6f42256b8b64501f22be7bade533f0c4
summary: Local web capability latencies and the user-agent refusal boundary
result: fetch_page example.com 0.81 s; view_web_page example.com 2.12 s cold browser, 13259-byte PNG; search_web 3 results 1.91 s; local /check 9/9 free plus 1/1 credit. Wikipedia returns 403 to a browser-shaped agent, to curl and to a descriptive agent without contact, and 200 (441 KB) to name/version (contact); five other sites returned 200 with the browser string and were unaffected by extra browser headers. Four Firecrawl credits spent of 1000/month.
decision: Keep the browser-shaped agent as the default and add one retry with an optional self-identifying WEB_FALLBACK_USER_AGENT, empty by default. Deployed latencies remain unmeasured because nothing was deployed.

head: 280a781252beef3f1f139ea0e7c70fa7aafc313f
summary: Deployed self-test with the web capability, credit probe included
result: 10/10 in the deployed container: store.turn, store.memory, filesystem, browser.inspect, documents.read, documents.view, presentation.file, web.fetch, web.view (18265-byte PNG through the isolated renderer), web.search. 16.1 s wall clock covering both the worker's and the renderer's cold starts; render_web_page's first execution ever. Redeploy after the secret sync was 11.0 s with no image build, but the image inputs were unchanged, so the browser-layer cache claim is still untested. Two Firecrawl credits spent, six total.
decision: Roadmap queue 1 acceptance is met: every advertised tool passes in the deployed container. Renderer cold start is not separated from the worker's, and cloud-metadata reachability from the renderer container remains untested because our own policy refuses the address before the network is consulted.

head: 090a7091d7d5f78bd3c11969cc767cac97980f74
summary: Additive schema-2 migration on the deployed Neon database
result: Version 1 to 2 applied in place: user_state created, 5 conversations preserved, no reset. PostgreSQL store contract 42 passed in 119 s.
decision: Keep additive migration; a destructive reset stays behind the human gate and was not used.

head: 8e264e2ac5215cf6504abd892a306184532414d7
summary: Streamed request to assistant-llm-v2 (gemma-4-12b-it, vllm 0.26.0), stream_options.include_usage, three requests in one wake window
result: First SSE line 9.50 s cold (GPU wake included), 0.31 s and 0.30 s warm; tool calls fragmented by index with id+name in the opening chunk; finish_reason stop/tool_calls in an empty-delta chunk; usage in a choices-empty chunk; no reasoning_content emitted
decision: Streaming tool calls are usable as-is, so the answer-streaming design needs no fallback to non-streaming tool requests

head: 959d682c38e6c0f08b2a2c73bb76a567d09c90b2
summary: First measured baseline of four live deployed Telegram turns (2026-08-29, run ids 9b861f1e/a7b50f07/31deb3c3/fcd7dd26)
result: Per turn: 2 model calls (router + answer). Router input tokens 2452/2478/1190/1529 against the answer's 4936/4962/3674/4013, so routing costs about a third of a turn's input. Provider TTFT per call 2293/140/586/355 ms, while first visible response measured from the person's message was 14605/6526/2245/4088 ms - the gap is queue wait (6466/5272/241/908 ms), worker cold start and the router, not decoding. Total 15771/14151/9356/8562 ms. Persist 643/5636/36/584 ms, one outlier. Zero tool calls across all four.
decision: Item 5's single-call change now has a measured target; decode-side optimization does not. Recorded as the baseline item 4 changes are compared against.

head: 303b130664fccdd92b4e8b73e464f0ccfd5d6a21
summary: Decode throughput of Gemma 4 12B on an A10, vLLM 0.26.0, from engine metrics
result: Time per output token 21.2-23.9 ms across every input size; scenario A generated 512 tokens in 10.84 s of decode, about 47 tok/s. The 15-17 tok/s previously quoted was end to end and conflated network, prefill and decode.
decision: Stop quoting 15-17 tok/s as decode. Decode-side optimization has less headroom than that figure implied.

head: 303b130664fccdd92b4e8b73e464f0ccfd5d6a21
summary: Prefill scaling with input size on the same endpoint
result: 853 tokens 352 ms, 3285 tokens 1356 ms, 6528 tokens 2881 ms, 9773 tokens 4689 ms. Prefill throughput falls from 2425 to 2084 tok/s, so an 11.5x longer prompt costs 13.3x more prefill. At ~12k input a request spends 4.69 s in prefill against 0.64 s in decode.
decision: Treat context length as a latency cost, not only a VRAM cost. The router's second full-context request is about 1.0 s of unavoidable prefill per turn, which is queue item 5's measured target.

head: 303b130664fccdd92b4e8b73e464f0ccfd5d6a21
summary: Prefix cache effectiveness, measured rather than assumed
result: The same 3277-token prefix asked a second question: 3200 tokens served from cache (98%), KV computation 3277 -> 77 tokens, prefill 1370 -> 82 ms (16.8x), end to end 1402 -> 621 ms. Control requests with per-run unique markers recorded zero hits, so the prefill scaling above is real prefill.
decision: Prefix caching is confirmed active and large. Keep the system prompt and context prefix stable, and prefer prefix reuse over decode-side tuning.

head: 7317b9b5f5c936c6e5eae3db00efea1cf67fcec0
summary: First measurement of the primary metric: GPU active seconds per successful turn
result: Over the first six live turns on the deployed control plane: 21.22 s of derived GPU active time and $0.0065 per successful turn, 3.00 model calls, 1.00 tool calls, 5616 input and 282 output tokens per successful turn. Derived as model span plus the 12 s idle window, an upper bound, never billed.
decision: This is the baseline item 4's loop changes are compared against. Report it as derived and never sum it against Modal's invoice.

head: bdb4438b6b11a988e76770dba1a495b80508f21d
summary: Deployed-schema verification of the conversation lease before first traffic
result: Both claim statements plan against the live table: key lookup as an index scan on the primary key (cost 0.14..8.16), the lease as an Update (cost 16.49..24.52). Migration additive, no rewrite.
decision: Plan unproven SQL with EXPLAIN before deploying it when the contract suite has no database to run against.

head: e9917a9d50d4276b789349fc4d7e7033f02f1936

head: f433032fc31e88584defac95e090254f2b659d67
summary: Raised the model endpoint context ceiling from 16384 to 65536 on assistant-llm-v2 (A10, gpu_memory_utilization 0.80, unquantized KV)
result: Boot succeeded. Available KV cache memory 11.13 GiB, GPU KV cache size 256,669 tokens, maximum concurrency 3.92x at 65,536 tokens per request. 299.7 s request-to-serving for snapshot creation; text, image and audio all answered on the new revision. NCCL Broken-pipe warning storm absent after the boot (loopback rendezvous applied). Predicted concurrency was 1.32x from a 137 KB/token constant derived at the 16k ceiling; that constant does not hold across ceilings for this model, so the real headroom is about 3x the prediction and the recorded claim that 128k is unreachable on an A10 was withdrawn. vLLM also reported that CUDA graph memory profiling makes 0.80 equivalent to 0.7640 under older accounting, with 0.8360 restoring the previous effective pool.
decision: Keep the ceiling at 65536 and utilization at 0.80; do not quantize KV; read the pool size from the boot log rather than deriving a per-token constant.
